title: Your business. A little more help.
body: Run Your Business on AI · Jimmy Davis + Paul Lorkowski · September 10, 2026
note: Paul welcomes the room. Scan once and keep this page open. Phone optional; paper works too.

title: You do not need a clever question.
body: Tell us what your week looks like. We will help you find a place to start.
note: Launch the Where are you with AI? poll, then the work-interruption poll. Treat every answer as useful.

title: Free tools. An optional next step.
body: We will explain how to work with us near the end. Most people will use the free tools. No deposits tonight.
note: Both partners state why the event is free. No new payment terms or unsupported outcome promises.

title: The work wrapped around the work.
body: A customer to meet. A phone that keeps ringing. Another quote that pulls you off the road.
note: Paul tells his own logistics story. Do not claim a measured AI improvement in that business.

title: Better for whom?
body: Before we rewrite a website, we find out what the customer needs to hear.
note: Paul interviews the volunteer. Jimmy writes the customer brief. Separate facts, customer words, and guesses.

title: Same AI. A much better brief.
body: A vague request gets a vague first draft. Give it a real customer, a real job, and facts it can use.
note: Show two prompts against the same approved input. Compare the output; do not claim every model will behave identically.

title: Try one useful thing with us.
body: Choose a customer message or the first-job exercise. Add your own details. You can watch first.
note: Send the selected tool to phones. Jimmy demonstrates; Paul checks who has a usable result. Work in pairs if needed.

title: What would you try this on next?
body: We are back at 8:10. Keep your draft. Drop a question into the event page.
note: Leave the QR visible. Do not turn the reset into an extra presentation.

title: Would you actually use that?
body: Turn rough notes into a clean next step. Then check every detail against the original.
note: Paul leads CRM notes. Use an anonymized consenting example or label the fictional fallback. Nothing is sent or synced.

title: One job. Clear rules. Your approval.
body: Give the helper something small enough to test. Keep the judgment that belongs to you.
note: Feature Teach your first AI helper. First-job tool is the default for unsure attendees.

title: Worth trying, or another rabbit hole?
body: Can it do one job you care about, with facts you can check, and less work than before?
note: Open the 60-second guide. No recommendation to buy anything based on a score.

title: What still needs an answer?
body: Your business question is welcome. Keep client names and private details out.
note: Paul selects moderated questions. Show only approved text. Do not project private intake information.

title: Let’s see if there is a fit.
body: A short conversation with Jimmy and Paul is the next step. No money changes hands tonight.
note: Explain only the agreed audit offer. Use the verified booking route once provided; no invented scheduling link.

title: Go try one thing.
body: Save your tools. Write your first step. Then tell us what happened.
note: Launch the Friday poll, help owners save their notes, and finish at 9:00. Thank them whether they hire you or not.
